Note::TexAccessor::figures¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::figures() const

Extract Complete Figure Regions¶

figures() extracts complete figure and figure* environments from every Text cell. Each token contains the entire region, from \begin{...} through the matching \end{...}. Retaining the delimiters matters when a caller wants to relocate, inspect, or separately transform a float: the environment kind and its body remain one unit.

The two environment spellings are returned in source order. figure* is not treated as an ordinary figure, and an escaped opener such as \\begin{figure} does not start a region. A same-name environment nested in another is balanced as part of the outer token rather than terminating it at the first closer. An opener without a matching closer contributes no token; the method never fabricates a missing \end command.

This is structural extraction, not graphics discovery. It does not read image files, render TeX, or require a \caption or \includegraphics command in the body. Use includes() when only external paths are needed, captions() when only caption text is needed, or strip_figs() when the regions should be removed from otherwise retained source.

The result is ragged. tokens() is one flat Text Note; offsets() is an Int64 Note with one boundary per receiver cell plus a final boundary. Cell i owns the half-open range [offsets[i], offsets[i + 1]). The receiver’s rank is therefore represented by lane order and offsets, not copied onto the token Note. Undefined input returns undefined tokens and canonical offsets [0]; any defined non-Text dtype is rejected.

Scanning is linear in the source bytes plus the bytes copied into extracted regions. Nested same-name figures require only a depth counter; no document tree is built.

Example 1: Preserve Variant And Document Order¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\begin{figure*}wide\end{figure*} then \begin{figure}plain\end{figure})",
    R"(\begin{figure}outer \begin{figure}inner\end{figure} tail\end{figure})",
    R"(\begin{figure}unfinished)",
    R"(\\begin{figure}escaped\end{figure})"});
const auto blocks = source.tex().figures();

std::cout << blocks.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["\\begin{figure*}wide\\end{figure*}", "\\begin{figure}plain\\end{figure}", "\\begin{figure}outer \\begin{figure}inner\\end{figure} tail\\end{figure}"]

The starred block remains first. The nested ordinary figure belongs to one balanced outer token. Neither the unmatched opener nor the escaped opener produces a token.

Example 2: Recover Cell Ownership¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = blocks.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 2, 3, 3, 3]

The first cell owns two blocks, the second owns one, and the final two cells own empty ranges.

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Input¶

const auto absent = pluss::Note::undefined().tex().figures();
std::cout << std::boolalpha << absent.tokens().defined() << " offsets=["
          << absent.offsets().integers()[0] << "]\n";

try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().figures();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "figures Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false offsets=[0]
figures Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • captions: extract caption bodies without their float regions.

  • includes: extract external input and graphics paths.

  • strip_figs: remove complete figure regions from each cell.
